correctness.rationale: The analytic proof reconstructs the exact open parameter interval of exponents, the additive Bloch norm, an explicit boundary Beta integral, compact dilated-Hilbert approximants with an upper bound, and weakly-null little-Bloch spikes with matching lower bound. The nonstandard weak-null step uses the isometric closed embedding into C0(D) and measure duality; the spike rescaling is dominated by the integrable \(u^{1-\alpha}/(1+u/2)^2\). The numeric checker supplements but does not prove the infinite-dimensional statement.

value.rationale: The essential norm is a canonical Calkin-algebra invariant for a natural bounded singular integral on the full nonclassical Bloch parameter interval. Computing it exactly distinguishes noncompact boundary transfer from any possible interior norm amplification, complements the recent full-operator-norm classification, and gives the sharp unavoidable compact-approximation error at every alpha. It is not a textbook deduction from an operator-norm calculation because the sharp weakly-null obstruction must be established.
